146141a1d51e9ed5.title: Malcolm Todd: Do That Again Tour
146141a1d51e9ed5.desc: When Malcolm Todd graduated high school in 2022, he told his parents he would be taking a gap year to pursue music. They, unsurprisingly, were less than thrilled by the proclamation, but gave him a year to see if it could work. They learned what the rest of the music industry quickly realized: never bet against Malcolm Todd. “Every single day since I told my mom I wanted to do this, I have actively worked to grow my fanbase, to get better at music, to build this world,” he explains. By the time he shared Sweet Boy in 2024, his day job at Cold Stone was in the rearview. Tracks like “Roommates” were racking up millions of streams daily. Fast forward a year, and Todd is more motivated than ever on his self-titled album, a declaration that he isn’t a hype machine or a flash in the pan, but a generation-defining voice. That ambition is immediate on “Bleed,” the first single from Malcolm Todd. It features Omar Apollo, who serves as the lone guest on the album. Buoyed by a bouncy bassline, crisp drums, and an intoxicating synth melody, Malcolm and his frequent collaborators Jonah Cochran and Charlie Ziman, tried to make something as poppy as they possibly could. With most of the album…

14f49c7118fd75d5.title: Allan Rayman
14f49c7118fd75d5.desc: “Whoever Allan Rayman is, he’s made a hell of a body of work so far. The Wyoming born, Toronto based artist has delivered one head-scratching, hypnotic and heavenly project after another, including Hotel Allan [2016], Courtney EP [2017], Roadhouse 01 [2017], Harry Hard-On [2018], and CHRISTIAN [2020]. Along the way, he’s generated over 250 million streams, sold out tours in Europe, the United States and Canada, and shined at festivals including Reading & Leads, Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza, Ohana, Austin City Limits, and Osheaga. In the midst of this whirlwind, he gained a newfound clarity and applied it to finishing the upcoming album, ROADHOUSE 02, during the Global Pandemic. The long wait for ROADHOUSE 2 finally comes to an end as it will be released on March 18th.”

1491a00feed72096.title: 49th Annual Oktoberfest
1491a00feed72096.desc: Every fall, Old World Huntington Beach transforms into one of Southern California’s most iconic seasonal celebrations with its long-running annual Oktoberfest. Running since 1978, the festival has become a decades-old Huntington Beach tradition, bringing together authentic German food, imported beer, live bands, dancing, festival games, and a lively Bavarian atmosphere for locals and visitors alike. The 49th annual Oktoberfest at Old World will take place from September 12 through November 8, 2026, featuring themed nights, family-friendly experiences, traditional entertainment, and one of the largest Oktoberfest celebrations in Orange County. Guests can experience everything from stein-holding competitions and bratwurst feasts to lederhosen, dirndls, and live German music inside the festive Biergarten atmosphere. Inspired by the spirit of Munich’s world-famous celebration, Oktoberfest at Old World blends German heritage with Southern California culture, making it a must-visit fall destination in Huntington Beach for groups, couples, tourists, and families looking to celebrate the season.
